title: Magic, Muppets & Medicine
description: Six very specific rounds: the Muppets' big-screen adventures, 90s Disney classics, Tolkien's Middle-earth, C.S. Lewis's Narnia, the legendary 1969 Woodstock festival, and a pharmaceutical name-that-drug challenge.

questions.question: 'It's Not Easy Being Green' is the signature song of this amphibious Muppet, host of The Muppet Show and creator Jim Henson's most beloved character.
In 'The Muppet Christmas Carol' (1992), this Oscar-winning British actor played Ebenezer Scrooge while his co-stars were made of foam and fabric.
In 'Muppet Treasure Island' (1996), the role of the villainous Long John Silver went to this human actor, also famous for 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' and 'IT.'
This wild, drum-obsessed Muppet — whose vocabulary barely extends beyond one-word exclamations — is the explosive percussionist of Dr. Teeth and the Electric Mayhem.
In 'Muppets from Space' (1999), this blue, hook-nosed Muppet finally learns the truth about himself: he is an extraterrestrial and is reunited with his alien family.
In this 1992 Disney film set in the fictional kingdom of Agrabah, a street thief falls in love with a princess and uses three wishes from a fast-talking genie voiced by Robin Williams.
This 1991 Disney film became the first animated feature ever nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture, featuring a cursed prince, a bookworm named Belle, and an enchanted rose.
questions.answer: What is Beauty and the Beast?

questions.question: Released in 1998, this Disney film follows a young woman who disguises herself as a male soldier to serve in the Imperial Chinese Army in her ailing father's place.
Musician Phil Collins wrote and performed every song on the soundtrack of this 1999 Disney film about a boy raised by gorillas in the African jungle.
Based on a Victor Hugo novel, this 1996 Disney film follows bell ringer Quasimodo, who defends the gypsy Esmeralda against the sinister Judge Frollo in medieval Paris.
questions.answer: What is The Hunchback of Notre Dame?

questions.question: This Dark Lord forged the One Ring in the fires of a volcano in Mordor — and his power is so bound to it that its destruction would mean his own end.
Once the head of the Istari order and Gandalf's superior, this wizard betrayed the Fellowship of the Ring and allied himself with the forces of darkness.
Peter Jackson's 'The Return of the King' swept the 2004 Academy Awards, winning in every single category for which it was nominated — tying the all-time Oscar record shared with Ben-Hur and Titanic.
The One Ring can only be destroyed in the fires of this volcanic mountain inside Mordor — the very same place where it was originally forged.
J.R.R. Tolkien was a professor of Anglo-Saxon — and later Merton Professor of English Language and Literature — at this British university, where he developed the languages and lore of Middle-earth.
In C.S. Lewis's most famous Narnia book, young Lucy Pevensie first discovers the magical land by stepping through the back of this ordinary piece of furniture in the Professor's country house.
This great lion — the creator and true king of Narnia — willingly gives his life on the Stone Table and returns from the dead, serving as C.S. Lewis's Christ-like figure.
The White Witch's spell ensures it is 'always winter but never' this annual celebration — trapping Narnia in a hundred years of joyless cold.
C.S. Lewis's beloved fantasy series runs to this many books in total, from 'The Magician's Nephew' to 'The Last Battle.'
This valiant talking mouse sails to the very edge of the world in 'The Voyage of the Dawn Treader' — eventually crossing into Aslan's own country.
The original Woodstock festival was held in August 1969 on the dairy farm of this New York farmer, whose land hosted nearly half a million people.
This guitarist closed the Woodstock festival with a legendary, psychedelic performance of 'The Star-Spangled Banner' that remains one of rock history's most iconic moments.
Often called the 'Queen of Rock and Roll,' this blues singer delivered a powerful Woodstock set before dying of a drug overdose just over a year later.
During this British band's Woodstock set, activist Abbie Hoffman stormed the stage to make a speech — only to be driven off by guitarist Pete Townshend hitting him with his instrument.
The 1970 Woodstock documentary, directed by Michael Wadleigh, pioneered this filmmaking technique of showing multiple images simultaneously in the same frame — and won the Oscar for Best Documentary.
The active ingredient in Tylenol, this over-the-counter pain reliever and fever reducer is the most-used medication in the United States and appears in hundreds of cold and flu products.
Sold under the brand names Advil and Motrin, this nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug is one of the world's best-selling pain relievers.
The active ingredient in Benadryl, this antihistamine relieves allergies but also causes drowsiness — which is why it doubles as the active ingredient in most over-the-counter sleep aids.
Known worldwide simply as aspirin, this compound was first synthesized by Bayer chemist Felix Hoffmann in 1897 from a compound found in willow bark — and its full chemical name reflects that origin.
Fluoxetine — sold under the brand name Prozac — belongs to this class of antidepressants, which increase the availability of serotonin by blocking its reabsorption between neurons.
questions.answer: What are SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors)?
